name: Storage Access API
plain: Lets an embedded third-party frame ask for its own cookies back.
meaning: When third-party cookies are blocked, a frame can ask to use its first-party cookies. A grant lets that embed recognise the person across sites where it is embedded.

access.prompt_ui: Safari: always prompts (Allow or Don't Allow). Firefox: prompts after a number of sites; grants last 30 days. Chrome: prompts unless the sites are in the same Related Website Set (auto-grant).
access.persistence: Per top-level site and embedded site pair; lapses after 30 days without interaction (Chrome and Firefox)
access.revocation: Site settings, clearing site data, Permissions API 'change' event
access.iframe: Frame must be the one asking; sandboxed frames need allow-storage-access-by-user-activation
steps: User interacts with the embedded frame
Frame can now send first-party cookies (SameSite=None; Secure)

limits.headline: Can ask to get its own cookies back when shown inside another site
limits.user_action: You tap Sign in or Allow inside an embedded box, then answer the prompt.
can: Ask for its own cookies in an embedded frame, such as a login or comment box
Get access without a prompt in Chrome if the sites are in the same set
Keep access for 30 days in Firefox
cannot: Get access without a tap inside the frame
See cookies that belong to other sites
Get access if you choose Don't allow
limits.reach_label: Only its own cookies, after you allow
limits.differs: Safari always asks. Firefox asks after a number of sites. Chrome asks unless the sites are in the same Related Website Set.

story.what_it_is: Lets an embedded third party frame ask for its own cookies back.

marketing.name: Storage Access API
marketing.pitch: Documents how an embedded site can ask the browser for access to its own cookies.

marketing.name: Introducing Storage Access API
marketing.pitch: Apple describes a way for embedded content to ask for cookie access while blocking tracking by default.

story.for_you: You may see a prompt like 'Allow this site to use cookies on other sites?' or you may need to tap inside the embedded box. Say yes and the embedded box may log in.
story.for_makers: It lets honest embeds like comments, chat and video logins keep working while browsers block tracking by default. It is also the place where ad and tracking firms ask for access.

use_cases.example: A comment box from another service asks to use your login so you can post.
An embedded video player asks for access so it can keep your login and settings.
A document or design tool embedded in another site asks for its cookies to open your file.
A work app embedded inside another app asks for access so you stay signed in.
A payment frame asks for access to recognise a returning buyer.
An ad or tracking company asks for access, and the browser decides whether to allow it.
A support chat widget asks for access to keep your chat across pages.

technical_bounds: Needs user interaction with the frame first
Denied if the person never visited the embedded site as first party (Firefox: in 30 days)
Cross-site storage not granted for other frames
